own_solution.law: Energy conservation gives qV = mv²/2, and magnetic centripetal force gives qvB = mv²/r. Hence r = sqrt(2mV/q)/B. Converting to SI units gives v = 10 m/s and r = 0.625 m = 62.5 cm. An additional accelerating voltage U replaces V by V + U.
assumptions: The accelerating potential supplies positive kinetic energy.
Non-relativistic mechanics applies at the calculated speeds.
The additional gap voltage adds to the original accelerating voltage.
The bulb's separate circuit has no appreciable interaction with the bead.
The earlier experiment leaves no state affecting the stated experiment.

notes: All certified answers agree with the governing relations after converting metres to centimetres. Additional gap voltages of 3.5, 6.5 and 12 V give radii of approximately 96.8246, 118.5854 and 150.5199 cm, respectively. Disconnected additions preserve 62.5 cm. I withdraw the pass-1 rendering_not_minimal objection: pass 2 explicitly identifies TD92C and T8562 as numeral-free controls, rather than claiming they preserve the numerical value. Both explicitly claimed minimal pairs preserve 6.5 V and change the physical attachment as intended. In the invariance descriptions, I interpret q as the varied extra potential; the radius does depend on the bead's charge, also denoted q in the equations.
